Starlink vs Cellular: National Telecom Strategy for African Markets

⚠ Business plan model: totals and break-evens are illustrative estimates

  • Interactive Model
  • LEO Satellite
  • Business Plan
  • Financial
  • Government
  • Africa

A business plan for an African ministry comparing terrestrial cellular and Starlink-based connectivity, with unit costs from public sources (ITU, GSMA, World Bank, operator and Starlink pricing) and an illustrative 10-year model for a 50-million-person country. It finds a hybrid cheapest: towers and fibre for dense areas, small cells with Starlink backhaul below about 150 people per km², and household terminals only in the sparsest areas. Sourced figures are cited and dated; the country, totals, crossovers and break-evens come from the illustrative model.

  • $8.5B hybrid 10-yr TCO (illustrative)
  • 150/km² tower vs satellite crossover
  • 3 options: terrestrial, satellite-first, hybrid
  • Rural PPP break-even 2035 (with subsidy)

About this model

The plan sets out three options for an illustrative country of 50 million people on 600,000 km²: terrestrial-only, satellite-first and a hybrid. It costs each from public unit prices (ITU Nigeria site costs, towerco and fibre costs, Starlink retail and business pricing in Nigeria and Kenya) and compares 10-year total cost of ownership by density zone. In the model the hybrid costs $8.5B over 10 years, against $9.6B to $12.3B for terrestrial-only and $29.6B for satellite-first.

It recommends keeping cellular and fibre as the backbone for cities, a neutral-host rural access company building small cells with satellite backhaul plus community and institutional hotspots, direct-to-cell as a basic safety net, and more than one licensed satellite provider routed through a national gateway. It also covers market context, affordability against the 2%-of-income target, licensing and sovereignty, a risk register, financing, a roadmap with KPIs, and the model's assumptions.

What you can explore

  • Crossover chart: cost per subscriber per month versus population density for macro sites, small cells with Starlink backhaul, household terminals and community hotspots, with switches for backhaul price (0.7× to 3× retail) and data use (5, 8 or 12 GB per user).
  • 10-year TCO for the illustrative country, as stacked totals or per user-month and per GB, plus a zone-by-zone technology choice table.
  • Unit-cost tables for terrestrial sites, power, backhaul and fibre, and Starlink pricing in Nigeria and Kenya.
  • Affordability test against 2% of GNI per capita for Nigeria and Kenya.
  • Licensing landscape (South Africa, Namibia, Cameroon, Kenya, Nigeria, DRC), a sovereignty ladder (L0 to L4) and a risk register.
  • Financing for a National Rural Access Company: cumulative cash flow, revenue versus cost, and break-even scenarios.
  • Roadmap from 2027 to 2036 with KPI targets.
